clue.text: Citizen's cross leaving prison

indicators.note: leaving says the cross walks out of the prison's name, so those letters go

parts.note: Brixton is a prison in south London
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A citizen with a grudge walks out of jail.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIXTON is a well-known London prison; take out X and a Briton is left. The 's stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Britain is one of its citizens, so the national name serves for a citizen.

clue.text: Successful fringe the start of our expansion?

parts.note: big means successful, as in making it big
bangs are a fringe of hair cut straight across the forehead

explanation.surface: A smart new haircut marks the beginning of getting fatter.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmological theory holds the universe began in one event and has been expanding ever since.

clue.text: Twice nightly? That's more than enough for old people

indicators.note: more than enough says the two words hold more letters than needed, so the answer sits inside them

explanation.surface: Performing twice a night is excessive, a weary actor complains.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Twice' and the start of 'nightly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe of East Anglia, led by Boudicca.

clue.text: Heading the wrong way? Kill headlight

parts.note: to off someone is to kill them
a headlight sends out a beam

explanation.surface: A driver going the wrong way is told to switch off the headlight.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off course means wrong, mistaken, whether navigating or reasoning.

clue.text: Orator condemned coercion on being rejected

indicators.note: condemned letters are wrecked, so what remains of the word coercion is rearranged
being rejected says the word on is thrown out of coercion before the shuffle

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A speaker is censured for pressure tactics that were turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being rejected' takes ON out of COERCION, leaving COERCI, which 'condemned' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was the most famous public speaker of the Roman Republic.

clue.text: One king's revolting state

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the king's letters are read backwards

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king; with the 's it gives an S

explanation.surface: One monarch's nation rises in rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a country, a nation state in the Middle East.

clue.text: Former journalist covering case couldn't stand

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: covering means the journalist wraps around the case

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is a journalist
a crate is a packing case

explanation.surface: An ex-reporter covering a court case found it unbearable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests a legal case but is a packing crate.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to detest or loathe, so the past tense fits hated.

clue.text: Poem about Ulysses essentially at end of Troy

definitions.text: Poem about Ulysses essentially at end of Troy

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, here the hero's name without its closing pair of letters

parts.note: Ulysses is the Latin name of the Greek hero Odysseus

indicators.note: at end of picks the last letter of the word Troy

explanation.surface: The epic poem tells of the hero's journey after the fall of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek name ODYSSEUS loses US to give ODYSSE; the last letter of Troy completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic tells of the ten-year voyage home of the Greek hero after the Trojan War.

clue.text: Prophet grasping complex metaphor is transformed

indicators.note: grasping means the prophet holds the rearranged letters within

parts.note: Moses is the Old Testament prophet

indicators.note: complex means intricate, so the letters of metaphor are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prophet's grasp of a complicated figure of speech changes him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is transformed' fits the verb sense, though the answer is also the title of Ovid's poem, apt in a puzzle full of classical names.
explanation.definitionFit: To metamorphose is to change form completely, like a caterpillar into a butterfly.

clue.text: Regular sections of toughened moulding

indicators.note: regular sections means every other letter of the word toughened, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A builder picks out evenly spaced lengths of hardened trim.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogee is an S-shaped moulding profile used in architecture and joinery.

clue.text: Forsyte heroine puts off cutting out article for Iris

parts.note: Fleur Forsyte is a heroine of Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga novels

indicators.note: cutting out says the article is removed from the word for postpones

parts.note: puts off means postpones, delays
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A novel's heroine keeps postponing the gardening and leaves the irises unpruned.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forsyte Saga is John Galsworthy's series of novels about a wealthy English family.
explanation.definitionFit: The heraldic lily emblem of France is a stylised iris flower, and the name is also used for the plant itself.

clue.text: Scot's cross, forgetting large work by Martial

indicators.note: forgetting says the letter for large is left out of the cross

parts.note: the saltire, St Andrew's diagonal cross, is the Scottish flag
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A cross Scotsman forgets a big job done in a military style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Martial' looks like 'warlike' but is the Roman poet Martial, famed for satirical epigrams.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial wrote biting epigrams mocking Roman society, so his output is classic mockery in verse.

clue.text: Army's misled about new German vessel's flaw

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the German word
misled letters are led astray, so the letters of Army's are rearranged

parts.note: neu is German for new

explanation.surface: Soldiers are deceived about a new German warship's defect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship after 'German', but here it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An aneurysm is a weak bulge in the wall of a blood vessel, a defect in it.

clue.text: A brave chap gutted about old Greek commander

parts.note: game means plucky, willing, brave

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, so the middle letter of the word for chap goes

parts.note: a chap is a man
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A courageous man is disembowelled near an ancient general.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the king of Mycenae who led the Greek army at Troy.

clue.text: Obvious hole in mission statement

parts.note: manifest means plain, obvious
O looks like a hole

explanation.surface: A glaring gap in a company's statement of aims.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto publicly declares an organisation's aims and policies.

clue.text: Guy, for one, saves time

indicators.note: saves means keeps safe within, so the time letter goes inside

parts.note: say means for example, for one

explanation.surface: Guy, an example, rescues the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man's name but is a guy rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy rope and a stay are both lines that brace a mast or tent.

clue.text: Violinist's first quartet offers list of options

indicators.note: first quartet means only the first four letters of the violinist's name are kept

parts.note: Yehudi Menuhin was a celebrated violinist

explanation.surface: A violinist's debut string quartet offers a programme of pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quartet' sounds musical but just means four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu sets out the choices available, in a restaurant or on a computer screen.

clue.text: Bunch of careless dairymaids knocked over lots

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so the letters are read backwards
a bunch of the letters of careless dairymaids are taken from within them

explanation.surface: A group of clumsy milkmaids upset a large number of pails.
explanation.walkthrough: SDAIRYM sits across 'careless dairymaids'; 'knocked over' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Myriads are countless numbers, vast quantities of things.

clue.text: Kinky top, say, and liquid diet for goddess

indicators.note: say means the hairstyle's name is spoken and spelt another way

parts.note: an afro is a hairstyle of tightly curled hair, a kinky top

indicators.note: liquid means fluid, so the letters of diet flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for a fetish outfit and a liquid diet, aimed at looking divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives a word that sounds like AFRO, spelt APHRO; 'liquid' turns DIET into DITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite was the Greek goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: Man coming in behind Democrat tried again

indicators.note: coming in means the man enters the word for behind

parts.note: the rear is the behind
he stands for a man, a male

explanation.surface: A man arriving after a Democrat attempted it a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like an indicator of order but is the noun, the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A case that is heard again in court has been retried.

clue.text: Historian of The Quiet American?

parts.note: tacit means silent, unspoken

explanation.surface: Who wrote the history of Graham Greene's novel The Quiet American?
explanation.walkthrough: The Quiet American is a Graham Greene novel; here it is split into its quiet and American parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was the Roman author of the Annals and Histories.

clue.text: Citizen of Crete and other island bans Catholic

indicators.note: bans means keeps out, so the Catholic letters are excluded

parts.note: Minorca is another Mediterranean island, one of the Balearics
RC is short for Roman Catholic
'n' is a casual spelling of and

explanation.surface: A Cretan and another islander outlaw Catholicism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' gives N, as in rock 'n' roll; Minorca is a Spanish Balearic island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minoans were the Bronze Age civilisation of Crete, named after King Minos.

clue.text: Try collecting flyers suitable for Banksy work?

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the flyers and suitable go inside the try

parts.note: a go is a try
the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is a body of flyers
fit means suitable

explanation.surface: An attempt to gather leaflets fit for a street artist's piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyers' suggests leaflets but means airmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Banksy is a street artist whose painted walls are a single piece of graffiti, singular graffito.

clue.text: Poet reverses vehicle into garden

indicators.note: into says the turned vehicle goes inside the garden word

parts.note: to hoe is to garden, to weed

indicators.note: reverses says the vehicle word is read backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A poet backs his car into the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garden' is the verb here, to work the soil with a hoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was a leading Roman lyric poet of the Augustan age.

clue.text: Banks avoid costing toxic compound

indicators.note: banks are the outer edges, so the first and last letters are left off

parts.note: costing means pricing

explanation.surface: Banks dodge calculating charges on a poisonous product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like financial institutions but means the sides of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricin is a lethal poison extracted from castor beans.

clue.text: CIA spies trained to guard old American stars

indicators.note: to guard means the agency letters surround the rearranged ones

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency

indicators.note: trained means put through drills, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: American intelligence agents are drilled to protect a veteran US film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'CIA spies' reads as one phrase, but CIA is the container and only 'spies' joins O and A in the anagram; 'stars' is the constellation, not film stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassiopeia is a northern constellation, a group of stars shaped like a W.

clue.text: Censor and tenacious orator originally

indicators.note: originally means taking the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A Roman official famed for persistent speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: Cato the Elder held the office of censor and ended every speech demanding Carthage be destroyed, hence tenacious.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Censor was a Roman statesman known for dogged oratory against Carthage.

clue.text: Passes out note in special courts

indicators.note: in puts the note inside the word for courts

parts.note: to court is to woo
N is note, as in the compass and musical abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone hands out a note in specialist law courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courts' looks like a noun (law courts) but is the verb, woos.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to faint, to lose consciousness briefly.

clue.text: Lover of 17 lives next door to a lecturer

indicators.note: next door to says the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer
is means lives, exists

explanation.surface: Aphrodite's lover lives beside a university teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is APHRODITE, the goddess whose mortal lover was Adonis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the handsome youth Adonis was beloved by the goddess of love.
